title: One Place That Says Stop: A Supervisor That Combines Every Monitor, Latches, Keeps Every Cause, and Never Gets Less Strict When a Fault Is Added

questions.question: What should a field of Inputs that nobody filled in mean?
options: The unsafe case: an Inputs of all defaults gave stopped, a cap of 0 and all six causes
questions.explanation: A forgotten field must not be a robot that goes on.

questions.question: A tilt warning (0.5 m/s) and a power share of 0.2 (0.4 m/s) are both present. What is the cap?
options: 0.4: the lowest cap wins, and both reasons are reported
questions.explanation: The limit bits were tilt plus power.

questions.question: A robot stopped for a tilt loses its link as well, and both then go away. What is the state?
options: Still stopped, with both causes on record, until a reset: refused while a cause remains

questions.question: Why keep every cause seen since the latch and not only the first?
options: The first is not always the one that matters, and a reset after one cause with another still there starts the robot towards a hazard the operator was not told of
questions.explanation: A log that says link lost sends someone to the router.

questions.question: What was checked over all 1024 combinations of ten conditions?
options: That a stop cause always stopped, and that adding a fault never made the mode or the cap less strict: 0 violations in 10240 additions
questions.explanation: Only the all clear was normal.

questions.question: What is the supervisor's job compared with the stop path of lesson 19-02?
options: The supervisor decides; the stop path and the hardware enforce, and must work even if the process with the supervisor dies
